Hi Sophie — great to hear from you and thanks for the diagram + redline. Short answers at a high level: Redwood will consider a BAA but our recommended paths for handling PHI are Dedicated (reserved capacity) or Private (VPC/on-prem). Hosted API is considered on a case-by-case basis and typically requires additional controls and a security review.

To help us assess quickly, can you confirm the following details?
- Exact ePHI elements you plan to send (a list is fine: e.g., name, MRN, DOB, vitals, free-text clinical notes)
- Whether PHI is transformed or pseudonymized before transit or at ingestion
- Expected throughput and retention needs (do you need any KV/prefix caching of PHI on our side?)
- Any third-party subprocessors MedSync requires (analytics, logging, monitoring)
- The redline items you most want us to prioritize (we can iterate on the BAA).

I pulled in our legal & product leads internally and looped in priyom and marcus on next steps. If Dedicated/Private is acceptable, we can fast-track a pilot plan and template BAA. If you need Hosted, we will need a short security intake and an exec-level exception.

Can you get back with the ePHI list and retention requirements? I can then route to Legal and Product for a target timeline.

Best,
Laura Bennett

From: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@medsynchealth.com>

Cc: contracts@medsynchealth.com, Aaron Cho <aaron.cho@medsynchealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-16T08:40:00-04:00
Subject: Re: PHI ingestion & BAA onboarding for MedSync integration

Hi Laura — thanks for the quick reply and the routing. Answers below and attached:

- ePHI elements: patient full name, MRN, DOB (hashed on our side if you prefer), encounter timestamp, vitals (HR, BP, SpO2), provider ID, brief clinical note (max 512 chars).
- Transformation: Our connector can pseudonymize MRN and hash patient identifiers before sending; timestamps and vitals remain in cleartext.
- Throughput: average 50 events/min during peak for a single hospital + burst to 200; retention: we prefer a 24-hour TTL on intermediate caches and no long-term storage at Redwood.
- Subprocessors: we use a telemetry provider (analytix.io) for delivery retries and basic metrics; we can request that be excluded from any PHI handling.
- Redline priorities: liability caps around PHI, clarity on breach notification timing, and a clause confirming minimal necessary processing and deletion on request.

Attached: updated PHI_data_flow_diagram.png (same name) and our redline v1. We do have SOC 2 Type II reports and can share the auditor letter if needed.

If Hosted is a blocker, we are open to Dedicated pilot for a single hospital to start. Let me know what Redwood would need to proceed.

Regards,
Sophie

Laura / team — quick read and recommended approach after product/legal sync:

Summary: MedSync's ask is reasonable, but our current posture is to sign BAAs only for Dedicated or Private deployments where we can ensure isolation and controls. Hosting PHI on our multi-tenant Hosted API is allowed only with an executive exception, additional technical controls (strong KMS separation, dedicated tenant routing), and SRE/infra review. Given MedSync's willingness to accept Dedicated for a pilot, propose we default to that path.

Technical notes:
- 24-hour TTL on intermediate caches: feasible. We can configure KV/prefix cache TTLs per-tenant; confirm we will not write PHI to persistent storage beyond logs (logs scrubbed).
- Pseudonymization: encourage MedSync to hash MRNs before sending — reduces risk and simplifies BAA terms.
- Subprocessors: we must ensure any telemetry provider is excluded from PHI pipelines. We can add an exclusion clause in the BAA OR require MedSync to use a non-PHI telemetry flow.

Legal action items (Evelyn):
- Use Redwood BAA template (linked) as the starting point. Ask MedSync to redline ours instead of us redlining theirs. We will push back on broad liability caps and require 72-hour breach notification.

Operational next steps (ownership):
1) Laura: propose Dedicated pilot and ask MedSync to sign our BAA template (link below).
2) Marcus/Product: confirm resource assignment for Dedicated pilot (GPU pool, routing policy, TTL configuration).
3) Evelyn/Legal: send the BAA template and propose contract timeline (2 weeks for initial redline).

Related links: https://redwood.example.com/legal/BAA-template-v3, HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/75921

I'll draft an email to MedSync offering the Dedicated pilot path and attach our BAA template. Laura, if you want me to send that out I can — otherwise I can hand to Legal to lead.

Thanks,
